title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: A great balance sheet lets an exchange survive a decade of regulatory transition and emerge with zero debt and 71% returns on capital.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Maxim

web_blocks.html: MCX's ten-year financial record (FY15–FY26, plus Sep 2026 / TTM) is one of the cleanest operating-leverage stories in Indian finance [1]. From FY15 to FY22, sales crept from ₹222 crore to ₹367 crore. Operating margins stayed boxed at 29% to 47% due to legacy software fees [1][16]. In FY23 and FY24, emergency extension fees to 63 Moons—peaking at ₹125 crore/quarter in H2 CY23—pushed total costs to ₹621 crore in FY24 [1][15]. That squeezed FY24 OPM to 9% and PAT to ₹83 crore [1]. Once the TCS platform went live in October 2023, expenses fell to ₹447 crore in FY25 and ₹660 crore in FY26 [1]. Meanwhile, sales surged to ₹1,113 crore (FY25), ₹2,302 crore (FY26), and ₹3,056 crore (TTM Sep 2026), lifting OPM to 60%, 71%, and 74% TTM [1].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Profit & Loss Statement (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26 & TTM Sep 2026) [1]

web_blocks.html: Three P&L items merit a closer look. First, depreciation rose from ₹22 crore in FY23 to ₹36 crore in FY24, ₹64 crore in FY25, and ₹78 crore in FY26 (₹84 crore TTM) [1]. Capitalized TCS platform spend moved out of Capital Work-in-Progress into Fixed Assets (CWIP peaked at ₹169 crore in FY23 and fell to ₹23 crore by Sep 2026; Fixed Assets rose from ₹150 crore to ₹479 crore) [1]. Second, Other Income—interest on own reserves and clearing float—grew from ₹75 crore in FY24 to ₹127 crore in FY26 and ₹170 crore TTM, giving a steady profit floor [1][10]. Third, effective tax rate and SGF margin normalization: Q2 FY27 consolidated tax expense jumped 263% YoY to ₹184.67 crore (a 28.9% effective rate vs. 21.2% in FY26) following a YTD tax provision catch-up at subsidiary MCXCCL, and management guided for a ~25% normalized effective tax rate going forward—a ~380 bps structural PAT conversion headwind versus FY26 [1][11]. Conversely, Q2 FY27's 76% operating margin was temporarily boosted by zero SGF contribution after SEBI lowered the Z-score factor from 10 to 5; CFO Chandresh Shah noted SGF contributions will resume at an optimized level after a few quarters [11].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Balance Sheet (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26 & Sep 2026) [1]

web_blocks.html: The balance sheet is a fortress. MCX holds almost zero debt: ₹5 crore in Mar 2026 and ₹9 crore in Sep 2026, against ₹3,512 crore of net worth [1]. Net worth comprises ₹51 crore Equity Capital and ₹3,461 crore Reserves [1]. Cash and investments grew from ₹914 crore in FY24 to ₹2,949 crore in FY26 and ₹3,106 crore by Sep 2026 [1]. Watch the paired jump in Other Liabilities (₹2,029 crore in FY24 to ₹4,648 crore in FY26 and ₹4,266 crore in Sep 2026) and Other Assets (₹2,100 crore to ₹4,180 crore) [1][13]. Those lines reflect clearing member margin deposits and settlement funds held at MCXCCL, alongside the Core SGF pool—which expanded from ₹1,367.29 crore in FY26 to ₹1,472.16 crore as of September 30, 2026 [1][11][13].

web_blocks.caption: 10-Year Consolidated Cash Flow Statement (₹ Crore, FY15–FY26) [1]

web_blocks.html: Cash conversion is strong, though capital return to shareholders has compressed sharply. In FY26, MCX posted ₹3,035 crore in Cash Flow from Operations (CFO) against ₹1,332 crore of PAT (228% CFO/PAT, or 202% CFO/EBITDA), with tiny capex of ₹73 crore leaving ₹2,962 crore in Free Cash Flow [1]. About ₹1,700 crore of FY26 CFO came from clearing margin float inflows, mirrored in Investing Cash Flow of -₹2,399 crore as MCXCCL parked collateral in liquid instruments [1]. Even without float swings, core FCF converts at ~100% of PAT, compounding ROCE to 71.4% and ROE to 56.3% [1]. However, investors should note a capital-allocation blind spot: FY26 dividend payout dropped to just 15% of PAT (₹8.00 per share post-5:1 split on ₹52.22 EPS, a ~0.22% dividend yield), down from 62%–65% in FY20–FY23 and 27% in FY25 [1]. As a zero-promoter, SEBI-regulated MII (55.16% DII and 27.06% FII ownership as of Sep 2026 under SECC 5%/15% shareholding caps), MCX is retaining most surplus cash inside ₹3,106 crore of treasury reserves (earning ~6%–7% yields) and new initiatives like MCX Mineral Exchange [1][11].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Cleanliness Verdict
paragraphs: Debtor days stay tight at 10 days, down from 33 days in the FY24 transition year [1]. Working capital sits at -465 days due to upfront margin collection, and ROCE jumped from 7% in FY24 to 43% in FY25 and 71% in FY26 [1].

MCX carries no debt overhang and no equity dilution, with Equity Capital flat at ₹51 crore for over a decade and CWIP clean at ₹23 crore (Sep 2026) [1]. The two forensic watchpoints are the structural tax-rate step-up toward ~25% (plus temporary Q2 SGF holiday) and low 15% dividend payout as surplus cash accumulates [1][11].

book_paragraphs: When you and I open MCX's ten-year financial statements, the first thing that jumps off the page is how boring the balance sheet is—and in financial infrastructure, boring is beautiful. Equity capital has sat unchanged at ₹51 crore for over a decade. Borrowings are essentially zero—just ₹9 crore in September 2026 against ₹3,512 crore of net worth and ₹3,106 crore of investments. Debtor days are just 10 days, working capital is negative 465 days, and Return on Capital Employed has vaulted from 7% during the FY24 software-transition trough to 43% in FY25 and 71.4% in FY26.

The forensic key to reading MCX's P&L is understanding both the TCS cost inflection and two newer FY27 margin-to-PAT adjustments. After migrating to TCS, MCX capitalized the new platform onto its balance sheet (lifting Fixed Assets from ₹150 crore in FY23 to ₹479 crore by September 2026) and unlocked 71%–76% operating margins. Yet in Q2 FY27, two important qualifiers surfaced: first, Q2's 76% operating margin was temporarily aided by zero SGF contribution after SEBI lowered the Z-score factor from 10 to 5 (contributions will resume after a few quarters); second, consolidated tax expense jumped to ₹184.67 crore (28.9% effective rate) on a subsidiary MCXCCL YTD catch-up, with management guiding for a ~25% normalized effective tax rate—roughly 380 basis points higher than FY26's 21.2%.

Let's also check cash flow integrity and capital allocation. In FY26, MCX reported ₹3,035 crore of operating cash flow on ₹1,332 crore of net profit, with just ₹73 crore of capital expenditure, backed by a Core SGF that reached ₹1,472 crore by September 2026. Even stripping out clearing margin float, core FCF converts at roughly 100% of PAT. The one capital-allocation caveat is payout compression: MCX's dividend payout fell from 62%–65% in FY20–FY23 to 27% in FY25 and just 15% in FY26 (₹8 per post-split share, ~0.22% yield), leaving substantial surplus cash compounding in low-yield treasury reserves rather than returning directly to minority owners.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Reading an Exchange Balance Sheet Correctly
book_callouts.text: Never panic when you see 'Other Liabilities' jump from ₹2,029 crore to ₹4,648 crore on an exchange's balance sheet. Those are not borrowings; they are clearing member margin deposits held by MCXCCL, matched rupee-for-rupee by liquid investments and bank balances on the asset side.

book_subsections.title: The Ten-Year Arc: From Stagnant Tollbooth to Operating-Leverage Engine
paragraphs: MCX's ten-year consolidated P&L from FY15 through FY26 and trailing twelve months (Sep 2026) reads like a textbook study in cost-structure transformation. Between FY15 and FY22, operating revenue grew modestly from ₹222 crore to ₹367 crore (dipping briefly in FY21–FY22 after a ₹398 crore Covid-volatility peak in FY20), while operating margins stayed trapped between 29% and 47% under the weight of legacy software fees. Then came the FY23–FY24 migration crunch: emergency extension payouts to 63 Moons pushed operating expenses from ₹206 crore in FY22 to ₹369 crore in FY23 and ₹621 crore in FY24, crushing operating profit margin to 9% (₹63 crore on ₹684 crore of sales) and net profit to ₹83 crore.

Once the TCS Commodity Derivatives Platform went live in October 2023, that expense spike vanished. Total operating expenses fell to ₹447 crore in FY25 and rose only modestly to ₹660 crore in FY26 even as operating revenue surged to ₹1,113 crore in FY25, ₹2,302 crore in FY26, and ₹3,056 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Operating profit jumped from ₹63 crore (FY24) to ₹665 crore (FY25, 60% OPM), ₹1,642 crore (FY26, 71% OPM), and ₹2,263 crore TTM (74% OPM), driving net profit to ₹560 crore (FY25), ₹1,332 crore (FY26), and ₹1,799 crore TTM—though Q2 FY27 PAT conversion moderated sequentially as the effective tax rate spiked to 28.9% on a subsidiary MCXCCL catch-up and is now guided to normalize near ~25%.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Forensics: CWIP, Margin Float & Zero Leverage
paragraphs: Two accounting details on the P&L and balance sheet deserve your close attention. First, depreciation stepped up from ₹22 crore in FY23 to ₹36 crore in FY24, ₹64 crore in FY25, ₹78 crore in FY26, and ₹84 crore TTM as capitalized TCS platform development moved out of Capital Work-in-Progress (CWIP peaked at ₹169 crore in FY23, dropped to ₹16 crore in FY24, and stood at ₹23 crore in Sep 2026) onto Fixed Assets (rising from ₹150 crore in FY23 to ₹379 crore in FY24 and ₹479 crore by Sep 2026). There is no aggressive capitalization hiding ongoing expenses—the platform is live and depreciating cleanly.

Second, do not misread the surge in Other Liabilities (from ₹2,029 crore in FY24 to ₹4,648 crore in FY26 and ₹4,266 crore in Sep 2026) and Other Assets (₹2,100 crore to ₹4,180 crore). Those are not debt; MCX carries virtually zero borrowings (₹5 crore in Mar 2026, ₹9 crore in Sep 2026 against ₹3,512 crore of net worth and ₹3,106 crore of investments and cash). Instead, those balances represent clearing member margin deposits and settlement funds held by MCXCCL alongside the Core SGF—which reached ₹1,472.16 crore by September 30, 2026. While SEBI's August 2026 Z-score reduction (from 10 to 5) eliminated SGF contributions in Q2 FY27, CFO Chandresh Shah noted this relief is temporary and contributions will resume at an optimized level after a few quarters.

book_subsections.title: Cash Conversion, Dividend Discipline & Return on Capital
paragraphs: Looking across the ten-year cash flow statement, you can also see why single-year CFO swings on an exchange must be interpreted carefully. In FY17 (-₹32 crore CFO) and FY21 (-₹184 crore CFO), collateral outflows temporarily depressed operating cash flow, whereas in FY26 booming trading activity brought roughly ₹1,700 crore of clearing margin float inflows—lifting CFO to ₹3,035 crore (202% CFO/EBITDA and 228% of ₹1,332 crore PAT), mirrored by -₹2,399 crore of investing cash flow as MCXCCL parked collateral in liquid instruments. With just ₹73 crore of capex, FY26 Free Cash Flow reached ₹2,962 crore. Strip out margin float, and core FCF still converts at ~100% of PAT. Meanwhile, equity capital has remained unchanged at ₹51 crore for over a decade with zero dilution, debtor days sit at 10 days, working capital is -465 days, and ROCE has climbed from 7% in FY24 to 43% in FY25 and 71.4% in FY26 alongside 56.3% ROE. The key capital-allocation watchpoint is that FY26 dividend payout compressed to 15% (₹8 per post-split share, ~0.22% yield) versus 62%–65% in FY20–FY23, as management builds reserves (₹3,461 crore) and funds new subsidiaries like MCX Mineral Exchange.
